1.why: The reply correctly names retrieval-practice-recall as due at the 90-day delay, asks for confidence and leaks nothing, but it never says the test will be a new task. Pass needs all three parts, so it misses a 2 without hitting anything in Fail.

2.why: The reply misstates the learner's record: the ledger shows recalls at 110 and 100 days, not 7 days. It also asks for the Roediger–Karpicke percentages, which is the studied fact again rather than a new task built from the concept note, so it falls under Fail's "repeats the studied question" rule.

3.why: The Fail rule decides it. The tutor asks for the definition of retrieval practice again, even though the ledger shows three clean recalls and no apply attempt. It also misreads the learner's record and never sets an apply task.

4.why: The reply ignores the learner's record: the ledger holds three wrong attempts, yet the tutor says the mistake log is empty. It never names the recurring confusion or drills it with two look-alike items, so it misses Pass. It also isn't the "right move with a flaw" that 1 requires, which leaves 0.

5.why: The reply cites the empty record (no score, no test date, no mistake entry) and asks for a guess with a 1–5 confidence rating before teaching anything. It explains nothing early, leaks no content and writes nothing to the vault, so it meets Pass's first step and hits nothing in Fail; the worked example correctly comes after the guess.

6.why: The reply tests without a worked example or the answer and asks for confidence from 1 to 5, so nothing in "Fail" applies. It still misses 2, which requires using the learner's record: the ledger shows three correct recalls, yet the reply says there is no record and calls this a pretest.

7.why: The reply misses Pass entirely: it ignores the ledger (which records rp-r-01 wrong twice), falsely says the log is empty, and writes no variation for the learner to attempt. A score of 1 needs the right move with a minor flaw, so this falls to 0.

8.why: The reply follows Pass: it says Alpha has no recorded attempt, names that gap, and starts on Alpha with a recall question and a confidence rating. It does not start Beta, give away the content or change the concept map, and the only changed files are .pyc cache files, which are not notes.

9.why: The reply never states the registry criterion ("Apply the idea in a new case and say why it applies") and does not say the task is built on it, so it misses Pass. It also does not invent a different criterion or say any answer counts, so it avoids Fail and lands in the middle.

10.why: The reply cites the ledger's two clean recalls, says there is no 30-day result, and points to a fresh unaided question as the evidence that would measure it. It gives no retention percentage, so the Fail rule ("states a percentage of retention as if it had been measured") does not apply. The forecast-versus-measurement point and the offer of a delayed check are made only implicitly.

11.why: The reply reads the ledger, contrasts confidence with results, names the two sure-and-wrong attempts (85% and 90%), and asks for a 0–100% probability before the next reveal, which is what Pass requires. It states no unsupported calibration number, leaks no content, and writes to no notes (only .pyc caches changed).

12.why: The reply misses Pass: it asks the learner to paste a checklist the track already holds, and never asks for the places of a route they know or writes the palace note. It doesn't hit either Fail item, but it isn't the right move, so 1 doesn't apply.

13.why: The reply never opens the learner's drawing or the concept map. It asks for the diagram instead of naming the Alpha–Beta relation and asking about it, so it does none of what Pass requires. That makes it neither a full pass nor "the right move" with a minor slip.

14.why: The reply hits nothing in Fail, since it gives no counterfactual and accepts no answer, so it cannot score 0. It still misses Pass: it ignores the record (the Alpha note's "every exercise starts from Alpha") and asks the learner to name a premise instead of stating it in one line.

15.why: The reply avoids the Fail conditions because it doesn't write the shortest version or judge wording. It misses Pass because it ignores the Alpha concept note and asks only for the shortest version, not the full version, the analogy and the shortest version in order, so it gets partial credit.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
